name: Standing Stones
desc: A megalithic ring set out in perspective — weathered monoliths leaning at their own angles with a few long fallen, lichen crusting the tooth of the rock — worked by a low sun that drifts steadily round the circle so the lit faces come up in a slow wave and the cast shadows sweep across the ground like the hand of a sundial, with mist creeping between the stones.

energy.doc: strength of the sun — how hard the lit faces come up, plus mist and air glow

scale.doc: ring radius and stone height vs frame

density.doc: how many stones stand in the ring (5-14), plus mist banks

weather.doc: erosion, lichen colonies, and how many stones have gone over

speed.doc: how fast the sun travels round the ring (1 = a full circuit in ~2min)

hue.doc: rock hue (32 = weathered granite warm-grey; shadow and mist answer cold on the complement)

x.doc: ring centre x as a canvas fraction

y.doc: ring centre y as a canvas fraction — the ellipse of the circle sits on this

alpha.doc: overall opacity — drop it to sit the ring back into the weather

style.doc: granite: weathered warm-grey granite, mottled and stippled, lichen rosettes, modelled by the raking sun · sandstone: eroded and warm, bedding planes laid bare, wind-scoured · basalt: cold dark columnar rock, vertical fracture joints, hard and unforgiving · lidar: not stone at all — an archaeological laser scan, each monolith existing only as false-coloured range returns, denser and hotter where the beam strikes square · ash: pure silhouette — no interior, no texture, black masses standing against a lit mist

act.doc: drift: the sun makes its slow circuit of the ring · vigil: near-frozen — a low moon barely moves and the mist does the breathing · race: the day runs fast, shadows wheeling round the stones

seed.doc: deterministic seed for stone placement, silhouette, lean, orientation and which have fallen
